newsitem.title: FRANCE: Pace to sell belly capacity on new Ryanair service.
newsitem.headline: Pace to sell belly capacity on new Ryanair service.

text.p: London Heathrow-based agent, Pace Airline Services, said it will be selling the belly capacity on low-fare Irish airline Ryanair's new Boeing 737 passenger services from Dublin to destinations in France, Belgium and Sweden.

"We already sell all the belly capacity on Ryanair's existing services, the majority between Dublin and around a dozen destinations in the UK and wiil be doing the same on the airline's new routes in mainland Europe," Pace managing director, Mac Warner, told Reuters.
From May 1, Ryanair will operate three daily frequencies linking the Irish capital with Beauvais and Charleroi, respectively 50 miles north of Paris and 40 miles south of Brussels.
Ryanair is to launch a Dublin-Norrkoping (Sweden) in June 1997 too.

"We are currently in the process of signing up sub-contractors to look after cargo sales and handling. While the flights will be operating from Beauvais and Charleroi, the freight "product" will effectively be sold ex-Paris/CDG and Brussels airports, trucking being included," Warner said.

The 737s which Ryanair are to deployed on the routes in question will be able to handle up to 1.5 tonnes per flight and are suited to small-scale shipments, computer parts being one example," Warner added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
